# Next-Iteration Design: Five Buildable Upgrades, Ordered by Value/Cost

## Framing: the single-point-of-judgment risk

Your current loop turns $1.48/day of frontier judgment into roughly 40 executed lanes. That leverage is real. It has one structural weakness: **a single verdict can reach every lane before anything measures whether it was right** [inference].

The $0.42 lensing verdict propagated through doctrine, the behavioral layer, and MCP-style propagation into about 40 lanes [report, your own receipts]. If that verdict was subtly wrong, all 40 lanes inherit the same error. Your second-family judge and gates check execution quality. They do not check whether the doctrine itself improved outcomes.

The public discourse shows why this matters. The Anthropic read (GLM-5.3 at ExploitBench 50/410, close to Mythos Preview's 56/410) and the CAISI read (GLM-5.3 generally behind on bug-finding) are two expensive, careful instruments pointing different directions [report].

- **Disconfirming note.** They may not actually contradict each other. Exploit development end to end and bug-finding are different tasks. A model can be strong at weaponizing a known bug and weak at finding one [inference].
- **Lesson either way.** Published verdicts are task-shaped. Yours are too.
